<thought>To synthesize the target stilbene, a single‑step Wittig reaction can be used. Commercially available p‑anisaldehyde (COc1ccc(C=O)cc1) reacts with the commercially available (4‑methoxyphenyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide (COc1ccc(P(C6H5)(C6H5)C6H5)cc1.[Br-]) to give the desired C=C‑linked product. Both precursors are inexpensive, keeping the total cost well below $150. The retrosynthesis tree therefore has one reaction node with these two leaf molecules.</thought>
